title: Only the sphere reads distance plainly at every size
claim: For networks of equally spaced rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts, the plain first need being on time when it comes at the directed distance: (1) every loop of rings and every pair of rings sharing contacts is on time at every size, and so are the five Platonic networks (exact); (2) the square plane has a late ring at distance 4 (its single closest contact reached by two shortest routes); the triangular and honeycomb planes at 6 and 5 (exact); (3) a quotient of a tessellation whose medial systole is at least 2l + m, l the cover's first late distance, is late; (4) hence the on-time tori are exactly 9 square lattices (index at most 17), 11 triangular (at most 21) and 6 honeycomb (at most 9), both chiralities; the smallest late regular map is the twisted torus {4,4}_(2,3) of 13 rings, whose mirror image is on time. Computed: in every cover read the first tie of shortest routes comes at tau = L - L/m - L/f + 1 (L = lcm(m, f)) and the first late ring at tau + 1 (tau + 2 for triangular faces and larger rings).
failure_conditions: A loop of rings or a pair of rings sharing contacts with a late ring, or a Platonic network with one.
A torus of index at least 72 (square), 81 (triangular) or 43 (honeycomb) that is on time, or an on-time torus missing from the lists.
A quotient with medial systole at least 2l + m whose image of the cover's late ring is on time.
foundation_claim_scope: Networks of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts that are regular maps, tori or loops, given rather than grown; the plain first need against the directed distance (A40, A41); two-time knots only (A30). The hyperbolic covers are computed, their formulas patterns.
